questions.label: Question 01
questions.question: A hospital has five years of patient records, each labelled “readmitted within 30 days: yes / no”. It wants to predict readmission risk for newly discharged patients. Which learning setup fits?
options: Unsupervised clustering of patients
Supervised binary classification
Reinforcement learning with a reward for each discharge
Dimensionality reduction with PCA

questions.label: Question 02
questions.question: A real-estate startup wants to predict the sale price in dollars of a home from its area, number of bedrooms and neighbourhood. Which formulation and loss are most appropriate?
options: Binary classification trained with cross-entropy
Clustering evaluated with the silhouette score
Classification evaluated with accuracy
Regression trained with Mean Squared Error (or MAE)

questions.label: Question 03
questions.question: A model reaches 99% training accuracy but only 72% validation accuracy, and 5-fold cross-validation confirms the gap. What is the best next step?
options: Reduce variance: add regularization, get more data, or simplify the model
Increase model complexity so it fits even better
Train longer with a higher learning rate
Keep checking the test set until the score rises

questions.label: Question 04
questions.question: A data scientist fits a plain linear regression to data that is clearly curved. Training R² = 0.41 and validation R² = 0.40. How should this be diagnosed and fixed?
options: Overfitting: add stronger L2 regularization
Data leakage: re-split the dataset
Underfitting (high bias): add non-linear/polynomial features or a more flexible model
High variance: collect ten times more data and keep the same model

questions.label: Question 05
questions.question: A spam detector built with logistic regression outputs 0.82 for a new email, and the decision threshold is 0.5. What does this mean?
options: 82% of the words in the email are spam words
The model estimates an 82% probability the email is spam, so it is classified as spam
The model is 82% accurate overall
The email is classified as not spam because 0.82 exceeds the threshold

questions.label: Question 06
questions.question: A genomics team has 500 patients and 2,000 gene-expression features; they believe only about 20 genes matter. They want an interpretable model that automatically selects features. Which approach fits best?
options: L1-regularized (Lasso) regression
L2-regularized (Ridge) regression
Ordinary least squares via the normal equation
k-NN with k = 1

questions.label: Question 07
questions.question: A k-NN loan-default model uses age (20–60) and annual income (20,000–200,000) as raw inputs. Predictions seem to ignore age completely. Why, and what is the fix?
options: k-NN cannot handle numeric features; one-hot encode them
Age must be removed because it is highly correlated with income
k must be raised to about 1,000
Income dominates the Euclidean distance because of its scale; standardize the features

questions.label: Question 08
questions.question: An analyst standardizes the entire dataset (mean and std computed on all rows), then splits into train/test and reports 94% test accuracy. In production the model scores 85%. What is the most likely cause?
options: Underfitting caused by standardization
The test set was too large
Data leakage: test-set statistics influenced preprocessing, inflating the test score
The learning rate was too high

questions.label: Question 09
questions.question: A retailer has purchase histories for 200,000 customers but no labels. Marketing wants natural customer segments. Which approach is appropriate?
options: Cluster the standardized features with k-means or hierarchical clustering
Train a logistic regression classifier
Fit a linear regression to predict spend
Train a decision tree to predict the segment name

questions.label: Question 10
questions.question: Running k-means for k = 1 to 6 gives these inertia (within-cluster SSE) values: 1000, 520, 280, 250, 238, 230. Using the elbow method, which k is best?

options: K-means with a much larger k

The 5 components are exactly the 5 most important original sensors
PCA must be rerun with labels to be valid
Project onto 5 components, keeping about 95% of the information in 90% fewer dimensions

questions.label: Question 13
questions.question: For one data point, the mean distance to the other points in its own cluster is a = 2, and the mean distance to the nearest other cluster is b = 6. What is its silhouette value and meaning?
options: ≈ 0.33: ambiguous
≈ 0.67: well matched to its own cluster
3.00: extremely well clustered
−0.67: probably in the wrong cluster

options: Use k-means++ initialization and several restarts (n_init), keeping the run with the lowest inertia
Switch to a supervised classifier

questions.label: Question 15
questions.question: A network trains normally with learning rate 0.001. After changing it to 1.0, the loss reads 2.3, 8.7, 54.1, then NaN. What is the problem and the fix?
options: The model is underfitting; add more layers
The batch size is too large; use batch size 1
The learning rate is too large and training diverges; lower it (and consider warm-up or gradient clipping)
The model is overfitting; add dropout

options: Full-batch gradient descent
Mini-batch stochastic gradient descent
Solving the normal equation
Computing one exact gradient on the whole dataset each step, but with Adam

questions.label: Question 18
questions.question: Training oscillates across the steep walls of a long, narrow valley in the loss surface and moves slowly along the valley floor. Which change addresses this directly?
options: Add momentum (or switch to Adam)
Decrease the number of epochs
Remove the bias terms
Use a constant, much larger learning rate

questions.label: Question 19
questions.question: A language model has embeddings for very rare words that receive tiny, infrequent gradients, and plain SGD with one global learning rate trains them very slowly. Which property of Adam helps most?
options: Using the full dataset for each update
Forcing all weights to have the same step length
Per-parameter step sizes from the second-moment estimate vt (bigger steps for small, rare gradients)
Removing the need for any learning rate

options: About 0.001 (decreasing it by η)
About 0.002
About 0.0005
About 0.004

questions.label: Question 22
questions.question: A team trains with Adam and an L2 penalty added to the loss, but it generalizes worse than expected. A practitioner suggests a change to the optimizer. Which is best?
options: Remove all regularization
Switch to AdamW, which decouples weight decay from the adaptive gradient update
Set β2 to 0
Replace the loss with accuracy

questions.label: Question 23
questions.question: A classifier on 200 samples gives TP = 40, FP = 10, FN = 20, TN = 130. What are its precision and recall?
options: Precision ≈ 0.67, Recall = 0.80
Precision = 0.85, Recall = 0.85
Precision = 0.80, Recall ≈ 0.67
Precision = 0.80, Recall = 0.80

questions.label: Question 24
questions.question: A cancer-screening test is reviewed. Missing a real case could be fatal, while a false alarm only leads to a follow-up test. Which metric/adjustment should be prioritized?
options: Precision; raise the decision threshold
Accuracy; leave the threshold at 0.5
Specificity only
Recall (sensitivity); lower the decision threshold

questions.label: Question 25
questions.question: legitimate email is much worse than letting some spam through. Which approach follows?
options: Optimize recall and lower the threshold
Optimize precision and raise the decision threshold
Use accuracy at the default threshold
Maximize the number of predicted positives

questions.label: Question 26
questions.question: Only 1% of transactions are fraud. A model predicts “not fraud” for everything and reports 99% accuracy. Which statement exposes the real problem?
options: Its recall for fraud is 0%, so it catches no fraud at all
99% accuracy proves the model is excellent
Its specificity of 100% shows it works well
Its F1 score must therefore be about 0.99

questions.label: Question 27
questions.question: A model has precision = 0.90 and recall = 0.50. What is its F1 score?

questions.label: Question 28
questions.question: A binary classifier achieves a ROC-AUC of 0.50 on a validation set. What does this indicate?
options: It is correct half of the time but otherwise useful
It is a perfect classifier
Its ranking ability is no better than random guessing
Its precision and recall are both exactly 0.5

questions.label: Question 29
questions.question: A rare-disease model (0.1% positives) shows ROC-AUC = 0.97, yet at 80% recall its precision is only about 4%. Which evaluation view gives the more honest picture for this class imbalance?
options: The Precision–Recall curve / Average Precision
The ROC curve alone
Training accuracy
The mean of TPR and FPR

questions.label: Question 30
questions.question: A fraud model’s threshold is lowered from 0.5 to 0.2. What is the typical effect?
options: Precision and recall both increase
Recall and FPR increase; precision usually decreases
Recall decreases and precision increases
Nothing changes because AUC is fixed

questions.label: Question 01
questions.question: A 5-layer MLP is built from dense layers that all use the identity (linear) activation. What is the consequence for the model?
options: It becomes slower to train but can still represent non-linear functions
All gradients become exactly zero
The whole network is equivalent to a single linear transformation, so depth adds no representational power
Its outputs are restricted to the range [0, 1]

Deep networks are never necessary because one layer is always sufficient in practice
It requires linear activations to hold

options: The gradients explode in the first step
Only the bias terms can be learned
